variants.headline: Assembly votes the government out
variants.sub: The government has been voted out by the Colonial Assembly.
variants.body:
The Colonial Assembly has voted the government out. It is a decisive parliamentary event, though it does not by itself describe what follows. An assessment of {target} should start with the withdrawal of confidence and avoid announcing a successor that this report does not identify.

Parliamentary responsibility must mean something when it is inconvenient as well as when it is useful. Our convictions require us to take the withdrawal of confidence seriously. Office is held within a representative system, and no political side should regard that system as merely an obstacle to itself.

We take a sympathetic view of {target}. A parliamentary defeat is decisive for office, but it need not be treated as a final moral verdict on every person or position involved. Political principle should remain visible when judgment becomes less comfortable.

variants.headline: Confidence withdrawn
variants.sub: An Assembly vote has removed the government in {colony}.
variants.body:

variants.headline: Office meets its parliamentary limit
variants.sub: The Colonial Assembly has voted the government out in {colony}.
